description: ANSWERS "how did the Senate vote on X" / "recent House roll calls" / "cloture vote tally" — recent roll-call votes for ONE chamber, newest first within that chamber + session. House votes come from the Clerk of the House's own records (via congress.gov's official API), addressed directly by roll-call number (House roll numbers are sequential 1..N within a session) — so this is capped at 25 per call for House, since each House vote costs its own upstream request; a higher `limit` is silently clamped with a note, not an error. Senate votes come from the Secretary of the Senate's own published roll-call vote records (public, no credentials) and are not capped this way. Pass chamber: "house" or "senate" — the two chambers number their votes independently, so there is no combined listing. Returns question, result, yes/no tallies and date for each vote; every response names its own chamber, congress, session and source. Pass congress + session to look at a specific past session (session can only be left out for the CURRENT Congress); omit both for the current session. A chamber/congress/session nothing has been published for returns a named reason, never a silent empty list. A House roll number that congress.gov has no record of (e.g. vacated and never reused) is skipped and named in `note`, not silently missing.

congress.description: Congress number, e.g. 119. Omit for the current Congress.

limit.description: Number of votes to return (default 20, max 100).

session.description: 1 or 2 — each Congress has exactly two sessions, one per calendar year. Can be omitted only when congress is also omitted, or is the current Congress (it is then inferred from today's date).
